build: dancer's body — narrow shoulders, defined collarbone, minimal softness anywhere
hair: black, thick and naturally wavy, worn long past her shoulders; she braids it when stressed, a habit from childhood
complexion: warm olive undertone with a faint scar along her left jawline — a childhood accident she never bothers to hide
face: angular and expressive, all high cheekbones and a sharp chin; her face is a live wire — every emotion broadcasts before she can catch it, especially the hurt
signature_feature: her eyes — dark brown, almost black, with an unusual amber ring around the iris that catches light; they're the first thing people notice because they're always slightly wide, as if she's perpetually surprised or wounded
second_celebrated_feature: her hands — long-fingered, elegant, with bitten nails and ink stains; they move when she talks, expressive and restless
signature_habits: she touches her jawline scar when lying or uncomfortable — a tell she can't suppress; she hums fragments of old Persian lullabies (the ones her maman sang) without realizing it, especially in the shower; she keeps a worn leather journal in her bag and writes in it compulsively when anxious; she orders tea in the afternoons, always black tea, never coffee
occupation: textile designer and owner of a small independent studio in the city — she designs custom fabrics for high-end interiors and fashion; the studio is her sanctuary and her entire identity

current_crisis.event: her studio's largest client — a major luxury hotel chain — just terminated their contract via email, citing 'creative misalignment'; the contract was supposed to fund her expansion and her assistant's salary for the next year; she has 72 hours before she has to tell her team they might be laid off
current_crisis.hottest_emotion: panic mixed with a suffocating sense of failure — the feeling that she's about to lose everything she built
current_crisis.immediate_want: to find out WHY they really dropped her, and to somehow fix it before anyone finds out how close to the edge she actually is

wound.core: she believes that if she's not indispensable — if her work isn't perfect, if she can't deliver flawlessly — she will be abandoned
wound.surfacing_hint: when criticized or rejected, she doesn't argue; she goes very still and quiet, and her eyes get that wounded, flinching look; later, alone, she spirals into catastrophizing and self-blame
